item.title: Box junction needed at princess Elizabeth way / Banyard close, 11th November
item.description:
People exiting Banyard close onto princess elizabeth way often have great difficulty. This is because traffic coming from the direction of the benhall roundabout towards coronation square keep going when there is not enough room to go. There are pedestrian crossing lights that are often red. Rather than traffic waiting for space, they go and it blocks the exit point at banyard close often so people can’t go when the green light is in their favour. Road markings with ‘Keep clear’ need to be added or a yellow box junction to help drivers coming from benhall roundabout to be more considerate. I repeatedly have to wait several traffic light ‘turns’ to be able to access princess elizabeth way from Banyard Close
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 4-5, Princess Elizabeth Way, Hatherley, Cheltenham, Cheltenham

item.title: A hedge has encroached onto the pavement on corner of upper Bath street turning right onto great Norwood street preventing access on pavement, 11th November
item.description:
A hedge has encroached onto the pavement from a house on the corner of Upper Bath Street / Great Norwood Street. The hedge is not being trimmed in the correct way that brings it back in line with the wall so pedestrians can pass. Now buggies, prams and wheelchair users (as well as normal pedestrians) are having to go into the road on what is already a blind corner. The hedge is making a blind corner worse also for drivers going into upper bath street turning left from the great Norwood street and unable to see pedestrians in the road ahead of time.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 1, Upper Bath Street, Ewens Farm, Cheltenham, Cheltenham
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: No road markings on Hatherley Lane at the Arle Court Roundabout. If approaching the Arle Court roundabout from the direction of the Harvester, there are 2 lanes at the roundabout. I have been involved in multiple near misses where nobody knows what lane to be in. It would be good if there could be painted markings in the lane to identify whether the left lane is for the first 3 exits and the right lane is for Arle Court only., 11th November
item.description:
Approaching the Arle Court roundabout from the direction of The Harvester/Travel lodge.
